# RFC 0002 Reproducible v0.1 preview contract

Status: adopted and implemented for the v0.1 working draft
Author: OEMS technical review assisted by Codex
Affected draft version: v0.1
Reviewed baseline: commit 9126bfa
Review date: 2026-10-09

## Problem

The initial fixtures have consistent arithmetic, but the draft does not yet specify enough evidence and population rules for independent implementations to agree on less complete inputs. This RFC records a technical review of RFC 0001, all five metric definitions, schemas, examples and fixtures. The review below describes baseline 9126bfa. The decision record adopts a bounded working-draft contract, now implemented in the specification, schemas and fixtures. Historical findings are retained for traceability.

### Verified claims

| Claim | Verdict | Evidence and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |

| The draft distinguishes DORA framing from OEMS calculation policy | Verified | [Overview](../specification/v0.1/overview.md) and the research-framing paragraphs in each metric definition. The DORA guide does not establish OEMS's committer-timestamp, cohort, median or deduplication rules. |
| The five JSON Schemas and supplied record examples are structurally valid | Verified within the checked inputs | Draft 2020-12 schema checks and 39 record/payload validations with explicit format checking passed. This excludes dataset metadata and metric outputs, which lack schemas. |

Lead-time observations are 3600, 7200, 10800 and 28800 seconds; their median is 9000 seconds. Recovery is 1800 seconds. |
| The complete fixture proves complete lead-time coverage | Unsupported | Nine of ten deployments have empty change_ids. The draft does not distinguish a confirmed absence of new commits from unavailable linkage. The four supplied durations are correct; their completeness is unproven. |

### Findings and release impact

“Blocker” means a decision is needed before claiming that the preview has a reproducible contract. Schema acceptance of a counterexample is not itself a schema defect: the draft deliberately delegates relationships to semantic validation.

| ID | Priority | Finding and concrete counterexample | Controlling draft evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | Blocker | Stable IDs and rollout_group_id do not determine when a phased rollout becomes effective or whether two deployment IDs in one service rollout count once. One region receives a new version and another fails: implementations can choose first exposure, rollout completion or exclusion. | [RFC 0001](0001-scope-and-design-goals.md), [terminology](../specification/v0.1/terminology.md), [canonical model](../specification/v0.1/canonical-data-model.md), [frequency](../specification/v0.1/metrics/deployment-frequency.md) |
| F2 | Blocker | Unknown qualification must be disclosed, but an unknown record may have effective_at=null. There is no rule for assigning that unresolved record to a window or deciding which results it prevents from being complete. | [Canonical model](../specification/v0.1/canonical-data-model.md), [deployment schema](../schemas/v0.1/deployment.schema.json), [shared rules](../specification/v0.1/measurement-rules.md) |
| F3 | Blocker | evidence_cutoff is metadata without a selection rule. Reconciled records have no collection/revision time. An episode restored after the cutoff is shape-valid; the recovery formula can include it unless an implementation supplies its own snapshot policy. | [Envelope](../specification/v0.1/event-envelope.md), [shared rules](../specification/v0.1/measurement-rules.md), [recovery](../specification/v0.1/metrics/failed-deployment-recovery-time.md), [complete dataset](../conformance/v0.1/cases/complete.json) |
| F4 | Blocker | Lead-time completeness cannot be derived from empty change lists. In complete.json, only d1 links commits; d2–d10 link none. History completeness does not prove link coverage. Distinct change IDs for the same repository/commit can also double-weight a duration because deduplication is defined by record ID, not commit identity. | [Lead time](../specification/v0.1/metrics/change-lead-time.md), [canonical model](../specification/v0.1/canonical-data-model.md), [change schema](../schemas/v0.1/change.schema.json), [complete output](../conformance/v0.1/expected-results/complete.json) |
| F5 | Blocker | The fail-rate research framing requires immediate intervention, but the failed classification has no operational evidence contract. Rework framing says unplanned, while the numerator uses incident_driven without defining whether that value necessarily means unplanned. Implementations can classify a scheduled post-incident improvement differently. | [Fail rate](../specification/v0.1/metrics/change-fail-rate.md), [rework](../specification/v0.1/metrics/deployment-rework-rate.md), [deployment schema](../schemas/v0.1/deployment.schema.json), [DORA guide](https://dora.dev/guides/dora-metrics/) |
| F6 | Blocker | Recovery lacks explicit consistency and quality rules: incident and causal deployment can name different services; onset can precede causal deployment effectiveness; the causal deployment can be excluded or not classified failed. Open and approximate episodes are mentioned but their effect on status is undefined. The unknown-classifications output marks recovery complete despite unknown failure classifications; the draft does not explain what completeness covers. | [Recovery](../specification/v0.1/metrics/failed-deployment-recovery-time.md), [canonical model](../specification/v0.1/canonical-data-model.md), [incident schema](../schemas/v0.1/incident.schema.json), [unknown-classifications output](../conformance/v0.1/expected-results/unknown-classifications.json) |
| F7 | Blocker | Incomplete collection explicitly suppresses settled frequency, but corresponding ratio and duration status rules are absent. Bounds over observed deployments can be mistaken for bounds over the true population. For example, 1 failure among 2 observed deployments does not establish a 50% population rate if 8 deployments are missing. Empty incomplete data also needs a status precedence rule. | [Shared rules](../specification/v0.1/measurement-rules.md), [fail rate](../specification/v0.1/metrics/change-fail-rate.md), [rework](../specification/v0.1/metrics/deployment-rework-rate.md) |

A one-hour window would currently count one calendar date, but some implementations may divide by elapsed days. ## Adopted rules

The sole-maintainer direction to progress the findings is recorded below. These rules are applied together in the specification, schemas, examples and fixtures. Wording inherited from the review is resolved by the implementation decisions below.

1. **Bound the first preview to reconciled snapshots.** Require a dataset-level declaration that records represent evidence available at evidence_cutoff. Include only revisions observed by that cutoff. Keep historical deployments needed for first-deployment detection. Treat restoration learned after cutoff as unavailable in that snapshot, leaving the episode open. Defer envelope/revision conformance to a separately identified profile rather than imply it is covered by metric cases. F3, F8.
2. **Define one production rollout per service.** Use a canonical service rollout identity; subordinate region, tenant and job outcomes cannot create additional counted deployments. effective_at is the earliest confirmed instant the changed version/configuration affects the service's production consumers. Later rollout failure does not erase production effectiveness. Canaries affecting real production consumers qualify; dark releases without consumer effect do not; an effective rollback is a separate rollout. F1.
3. **Represent unresolved qualification coverage explicitly.** Do not infer a window from observed_at or discard records with null effective_at. Require declared scope/time coverage for unresolved records; if coverage overlaps the requested service/window or cannot be bounded, disclose it and keep the affected population provisional. F2.
4. **Separate link coverage from history coverage.** Declare whether change linkage is complete for each qualifying deployment. An empty list with complete linkage means no new commit observations; an empty list with unknown linkage makes lead-time coverage provisional. Define change identity by namespaced repository identity plus commit identity, and reject conflicting aliases instead of double-counting. Keep the first qualifying deployment per change/service as the observation unit. Unknown history cannot establish a first deployment; disclose candidate observations separately from confirmed first-deployment observations. F4.
5. **Define classifications with reviewable evidence.** failed means a qualifying production deployment required immediate intervention such as a rollback or corrective hotfix because of its production impact. incident_driven means the deployment was unplanned and undertaken to remediate a production incident. Scheduled follow-up work is not automatically rework. Record a classification-specific source or review reference; a generic pipeline link alone does not demonstrate either decision. Define what immediate intervention means operationally without inventing a universal elapsed-time threshold. F5.
6. **Define recovery eligibility and quality separately.** Require a causal deployment for the same service, qualifying and classified failed; require onset no earlier than causal production effectiveness and restoration no earlier than onset. Retain the failure-onset cohort, explicitly an OEMS policy. Report completed, open, approximate and unresolved episode counts. Keep the completed-episode median separate from coverage/completion quality; do not label it a complete population measurement when known eligible episodes remain open or eligibility evidence is unresolved. Approximate completed episodes use a separate median and never enter the main median. F6.
7. **Define metric-specific status precedence.** Unresolved population/coverage yields provisional, including an observed empty set; complete known population with no eligible observations yields no_observations; otherwise complete applies only to the declared metric's evidence requirements. Preserve observed numerators and denominators. Label classification bounds as bounds on the observed qualifying population when collection is incomplete, and provide no settled full-population ratio. Apply coverage quality to duration statistics too. F7.
8. **Publish dataset and result contracts.** Add schemas for snapshot metadata and results, including service, window, timezone, cutoff, profile, counts, quality reasons and ratio population scope. Validate start<end, positive and consistent calendar_days, references, service consistency, timestamp order and natural-key conflicts in a separate semantic layer. Include context in expected outputs or define an explicit enclosing result envelope; consumers must not reconstruct it from a filename. F8.
9. **Restrict the first preview's calendar profile.** Use UTC whole-day windows only, with matching UTC midnight boundaries and validated calendar_days. Reject unsupported windows explicitly. Retain half-open boundaries: start included, end excluded. Add arbitrary timezones/partial-day windows through a later profile with tests. F9.

## Examples and counterexamples

- **Region fan-out:** one rollout changes regions A and B at different times. It contributes one service deployment, not two; first exposure versus completion must be a recorded policy.
- **No change versus no evidence:** a configuration-only rollout with confirmed empty commit linkage has no lead-time sample. A rollout whose collector cannot retrieve commits has missing evidence, not a zero-second duration.
- **Window boundaries:** a deployment effective exactly at start counts; one effective exactly at end does not. A causal deployment can precede the recovery window if failure onset falls inside it, subject to the accepted cohort rule.
- **As-of recovery:** with cutoff October 12, a restoration observed October 13 cannot retrospectively close the October 12 snapshot. A later snapshot can revise the result with its own cutoff.
- **Incomplete observation:** 1 failed deployment among 2 observed deployments with incomplete source coverage produces an observed ratio, not a known population ratio of 0.5.
- **Classification independence:** a planned deployment can fail without being rework; an unplanned incident hotfix can be rework without failing. A scheduled improvement after an incident is not necessarily rework.

## Alternatives

- Accept the current draft and leave these rules implementation-specific. This prevents an interoperability claim because matching inputs can yield different counts, populations and quality states.
- Require a full event ingestion/reconciliation profile immediately. This would address snapshot construction but expands the first milestone; a bounded reconciled-snapshot profile can be validated first.
- Support every reporting timezone and partial window immediately. This is useful but requires calendar validation, DST examples and an explicit frequency denominator policy before publication.
- Fail every dataset with missing evidence. This is simpler but loses the draft's intentional distinction between invalid relationships and valid incomplete evidence. Prefer explicit quality reasons and scoped provisional outputs, with rejection for contradictions.

## Compatibility and migration

There is no released contract to preserve. Acceptance will change draft metadata and expected outputs, and may add classification/linkage evidence fields. Update prose, schemas, examples and fixtures in one coordinated change. Do not silently reinterpret existing empty change lists as complete linkage. Pin implementations to the exact draft commit until a versioned preview is published.

## Privacy and security implications

Use synthetic fixtures and minimal namespaced identifiers/evidence references. Do not require personal contributor identity, private payloads or publicly accessible incident URLs. Evidence references must be reviewable by authorised consumers; validators must not fetch arbitrary source URLs. Snapshot retention, correction and privacy deletion still need a separately recorded policy; this RFC does not resolve that RFC 0001 question.

## Conformance and verification

Current implementation checks can be reproduced with:

```sh
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python tools/validate_v0_1.py
```

The original review passed 39 baseline record/payload checks. During implementation, an invalid-date rejection case revealed that the original environment lacked the optional date-time checker: requesting FormatChecker alone had silently skipped that format. The baseline was subsequently rechecked with the required format dependencies installed. The current helper refuses to run without date-time and URI checkers.

The current suite separately reports structural validation, semantic acceptance/rejection and full expected-result comparisons. See the conformance README for its coverage. It is a draft verification helper, not an independent implementation or a certification engine.
Implemented fixture coverage includes:

- Duplicate-identical records, conflicting IDs and aliases of one repository/commit.
- Start/end boundaries, production-effective failure, excluded attempts and one rollout with subordinate outcomes.
- Unknown qualification with/without time bounds, incomplete collection and observed-empty incomplete data.
- Repeat deployment of one change before/inside the window, multiple services, incomplete history, unresolved links and confirmed configuration-only changes.
- Completed/open/approximate recovery, recovery crossing the reporting window/cutoff, shared incidents and invalid causal relationships.
- Independent failure/rework classifications and scheduled post-incident work.
- Invalid dataset metadata, missing output context and explicit rejection of unsupported calendar profiles.

Keep structural validation, semantic rejection/quality handling and calculation comparisons as separately reported checks. CI runs those checked layers. Passing the present review script is not a certification or preview release gate by itself.

## Implementation decisions

- Production effectiveness is first confirmed consumer exposure, including real-consumer canaries. Excluded attempts have no production-effective timestamp.
- Canonical identities are service/rollout and namespaced repository/commit. Distinct aliases are rejected for reconciliation; identical repeated records are deduplicated.
- observed_at records evidence availability. Snapshots are closed-window results with cutoff at or after end; future observations/events are rejected. Snapshot construction remains an adapter responsibility.
- qualification_window supplies uncertain time coverage, or null indicates unbounded coverage when effective_at is also absent. Missing change linkage is explicit per deployment.
- Incomplete first-deployment evidence yields candidate counts and no confirmed lead-time median. Known classifications carry decision-specific evidence references.
- Approximate recovery starts use the causal effective_at and are reported in a separate median. Open, approximate and unresolved episodes keep recovery provisional. Unknown historical failure classifications conservatively keep episode completeness provisional.
- The first profile supports reconciled snapshots and UTC whole-day closed windows, known timestamp offsets and up to microsecond timestamp precision; leap-second notation and unknown offsets are explicitly unsupported. Other calendars and envelope-ingestion conformance are deferred, rather than left as unspecified behaviour.
- Dataset and result schemas, positive/negative fixtures and CI implement the three validation layers. Python helpers are optional tooling, not a language requirement for implementations.

## Deferred work

Snapshot retention and privacy deletion, provider-specific collection/provenance, other calendar profiles, envelope revision reconciliation and public conformance-claim policy need later bounded decisions. They are outside this implemented metric-input profile. Independent implementation feedback remains a stable-release gate, not a requirement for another maintainer to approve working-draft changes.

## Decision record

On 2026-10-09, Liam Gulliver, the sole maintainer, directed progression from proposals into implementation under sole-maintainer governance. This coordinated change records the bounded operational choices above and applies the reviewed rules to the working draft. The rationale is reproducible independent calculation without requiring an ingestion platform, a broad calendar model or a committee process at this stage. This direction adopts the draft scope in RFC 0001 and the operational contract here; it does not announce a release, accreditation or certification.
